papers.title: LIPUS promotes calcium oscillations to improve lymphatic drainage and alleviates cold-stimulated pain and effusion in osteoarthritis joints.
papers.authors: Yang J, Liu R, Yang X, Li X, Peng X, Han J et al.
papers.abstract:
Osteoarthritis (OA) patients in remission usually experience acute exacerbations of pain and joint swelling following cold stimulation. This represents one of the characteristic clinical presentations of "cold knees". In Traditional Chinese Medicine, this phenomenon correlates with "Cold Bi", reflecting "lingering dampness" and "stagnation of Blood and Qi" in the joints, and is conceptually consistent with dysfunction of synovial lymphatic system (SLS) observed in OA. However, the underlying mechanisms of cold-exacerbated OA and the therapeutic strategies remain poorly explored.
OA mouse models were established by destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) surgery. The mice were exposed to cold stimulation at 4 weeks post-surgery to mimic OA patients in remission experiencing acute cold stimulation. Joint pain-related behaviors were assessed using multiple approaches including gait analysis and von Frey test. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) was used to evaluate joint effusion. Near-infrared indocyanine green (NIR-ICG) imaging and intra-articular injections of Fluorescein isothiocyanate-dextran (FITC-dextran) were employed to assess lymphatic drainage. Furthermore, the effects of temperature decrease and low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) on calcium oscillations and nitric oxide (NO) production by lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs) were investigated using live-cell fluorescence imaging. Additionally, the mechanisms through which LIPUS plays therapeutic roles were also explored using transient receptor potential vanilloid 4 (TRPV4) inhibitor HC-067047.
Acute cold stimulation aggravated gait abnormality and decreased paw withdrawal threshold in DMM-operated mice. Furthermore, weight-bearing asymmetry and total locomotor distance in the open field were also worsened in these mice. The knee joint effusion was significantly aggravated following acute cold stimulation accompanied by impaired synovial lymphatic drainage. Mechanistically, cold stimulation suppressed calcium oscillations of LECs and decreased their NO production, which were efficiently restored by LIPUS. Additionally, LIPUS treatment improved lymphatic drainage of the knee joint and alleviated cold-stimulated exacerbation of OA phenotypes in mice. These therapeutic effects were significantly suppressed under TRPV4 inhibition as well as hindlimb lymphatic vessel ligation.
Dysfunction of lymphatic drainage contributes to cold-stimulated exacerbation of OA phenotypes in mice, which could be alleviated by LIPUS-induced NO production through the TRPV4/Ca2+/eNOS/NO axis. These findings provide novel insights into the mechanisms of "cold knees" and highlight the therapeutic potential of LIPUS in the treatment of pain and joint effusion in OA.The translational potential of this article: Our study suggests that LIPUS ameliorates cold-induced worsening of pain and joint effusion in OA by improving synovial lymphatic drainage. These findings provide preliminary evidence for the translational potential of LIPUS application in skeletal disorders characterized by lymphatic drainage dysfunction.

papers.title: Shexiang Huayu Xingnao Granule Alleviates Intracerebral Hemorrhage via PI3K/AKT-Mediated Neuroinflammation Regulation: Integrated Network Pharmacology and Experimental Validation.
papers.authors: RuKui Y, MingLi W, Chun L, MeiJuan C, Yuan Y
papers.abstract:
Employing network pharmacology prediction combined with experimental validation, this research elucidated the underlying mechanisms of Shexiang Huayu Xingnao granules (SXHY) against intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH).
Potential targets and related signaling pathways of SXHY acting on ICH were predicted through network pharmacology. An autologous blood injection-induced rat ICH model was established, with simvastatin as the positive control drug. The therapeutic effects of SXHY were evaluated using neurological function scores, brain water content, superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase, malondialdehyde activity, and brain tissue hemorrhage area. Mechanism studies used a lipopolysaccharide-stimulated BV-2 microglial cell model, assessing inflammatory mediator expression profiles and PI3K/AKT pathway modulation through RT-qPCR and Western blot analysis.
Network pharmacology analysis revealed 360 common SXHY-ICH targets, with 10 core targets (including TNF, AKT1, IL-6, and IL-1β) significantly enriched in the PI3K/AKT, AGE-RAGE, and MAPK pathways; molecular docking further demonstrated potent binding of the key component stigmasterol to TNF-α (binding energy: -9.125 kcal/mol) and IL-6 (binding energy: -8.57 kcal/mol). Animal experiments showed within-group improvements in neurological function from day 2 to day 3 post-ICH in SXHY groups. The observed proportions of animals with improved neurological scores were 88.9% (low-dose), 83.3% (high-dose), 70.0% (model), and 62.5% (simvastatin). However, no statistically significant between-group differences were observed at day 3 (p > 0.05). It also reduced brain edema (high dose: 78.0 ± 0.7% vs.
80.5 ± 1.0%, p < 0.01) and significantly decreased hematoma area (high dose: 0.35 ± 0.50 mm2 vs. model: 1.02 ± 0.93 mm2, p < 0.05); meanwhile, it significantly increased SOD activity (high dose: 68.7 ± 11.3 U/mg protein vs. model: 37.3±14.1 U/mg protein, p < 0.01). Cell experiments further confirmed that SXHY mediates anti-inflammatory activity through modulation of PI3K/AKT signaling, including reduced p-PI3K/GAPDH (p < 0.01), downregulation of proinflammatory cytokines TNF-α/IL-6/IL-1β mRNA (p < 0.01), and upregulation of anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 mRNA (p < 0.05).
SXHY may alleviate post-ICH brain injury by inhibiting neuroinflammation throu modulation of the PI3K/AKT pathway. The results provide new mechanistic evidence for traditional Chinese medicine interventions against ICH.

papers.title: Advancements in Natural Product-Based Ischemic Stroke Treatment: Mechanisms, Key Compounds, and Drug Delivery Systems.
papers.authors: Yang N, Li M, Wang M, Li X, Dong H, Yao J et al.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) remains the leading global cause of permanent neurological disability and mortality. Narrow therapeutic time windows and elevated hemorrhagic transformation risks restrict conventional clinical interventions, including intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy. Single-target neuroprotective agents fail to sustain long-term neurological functional recovery, resulting in unsatisfactory clinical outcomes. Natural products (NPs) derived from traditional Chinese medicine exert protective effects against cerebral ischemia via multiple pathways. However, their poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, low aqueous solubility, and inadequate in vivo bioavailability greatly hinder clinical translational application. This review systematically summarizes the pathological mechanisms of natural monomers for the treatment of ischemic stroke and four types of brain-targeted nanocarriers over the past decade. We reconstructed the pathological cascades of cerebral ischemia across the acute, subacute, and chronic repair phases, and critically discussed the inherent limitations of the middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model and existing monomer-based preclinical studies. This work provides systematic structure-activity relationship evidence and insights into nano-delivery strategies for the development of natural product-based anti-stroke therapeutics. We also propose future research directions, such as staged, sequential administration, precise multi-omics intervention, and standardized nanoformulation development, to accelerate the clinical translation of bioactive ingredients derived from traditional Chinese medicine.

papers.title: Artemisinin derived from Artemisia annua L. promotes thrombopoiesis via targeting FLT3: a novel strategy for thrombocytopenia management.
papers.authors: Mei X, Liu S, Zhou L, Wang Y, Hu T, Qi X et al.
papers.abstract: Artemisia annua L. (A. annua) has long been documented in traditional Chinese medicine for managing hemorrhagic conditions, attributed to its cooling and hemostatic properties. These historical applications suggest a potential role of A. annua in platelet-related disorders, although its hematopoietic mechanisms remain unclear. To investigate the thrombopoietic activity of A. annua, identify its bioactive constituent, and elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying its effects on thrombopoiesis. Chemical profiling identified major compounds in A. annua. MK differentiation was assessed in K562, Meg-01 cells, and primary murine haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs). A murine radiation-induced thrombocytopenia (RIT) model was used to evaluate in vivo efficacy. Molecular docking, drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), and signaling assays were conducted to explore molecular mechanisms. A. annua promoted MK differentiation, upregulating CD41/CD42b and enhancing polyploidization. Artemisinin was identified as the principal active compound. It promoted MK maturation in vitro and restored platelet counts, MK numbers, and HSPC populations in RIT mice without inducing systemic toxicity. Artemisinin also reduced bone marrow (BM) apoptosis and DNA damage while restoring platelet function. Mechanistically, artemisinin directly bound to FLT3 and activated the FLT3/MAPK pathway, leading to increased phosphorylation of MEK/ERK and upregulation of NF-E2 and TAL1. FLT3 and ERK inhibition abrogated these effects. Artemisinin is a potent thrombopoietic agent that acts via direct activation of FLT3 and its downstream MAPK signaling cascade. The findings identify FLT3 as a novel therapeutic target for thrombocytopenia and support the potential clinical application of artemisinin in radiation-related hematological disorders.

papers.title: Exosomes, a potential approach to enhance the therapeutic effects of traditional Chinese medicine.
papers.authors: Huang T, Wang Z, Zhao Y, Fang W
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) exerts unique therapeutic effects, while some unfavorable physicochemical properties limit its therapeutic potential. Exosomes are involved in cellular communication and may enhance the efficacy of TCM. The relationship between TCM and exosomes is supported by the connection between exosomes and the theory of "Qi, Xue and Ye" (one of the basic theories of TCM). Also, the functional resemblance between exosomes and Qi, which is less researched. We fill this gap by systematically summarizing exosomes from different sources with therapeutic effects and exploring the mechanisms and implications of exosomes in TCM treatment. TCM and exosomes undergo two-way communication, with TCM affecting exosomes and exosomes loading TCM monomers. The dual roles of exosomes as destructive agents in disease development are also emphasized; current obstacles and future scope of TCM-exosome therapeutic strategies are fully discussed. The objective of this review is to stimulate further investigation and create a new application of TCM.

papers.title: Panaxadiol derivatives inhibit lung metastasis of breast cancer via DLL4-Notch signaling pathway and palmitoyl carnitine aggregation.
papers.authors: Xiao S, Xu L, Liu L, Zhang T, Bai X, Li Z et al.
papers.abstract:
As a classic traditional Chinese medicine, ginseng is widely used in cancer treatment. We found that the panaxadiol derivative 6a inhibits breast cancer cell proliferation, but its anti-metastatic effect and mechanism remain unclear.
Multiple breast cancer cell lines were used to assess the in vitro antiproliferative and antimigratory activities of 6a. A lung metastasis model, small animal imaging, and pathological examination were employed for in vivo efficacy evaluation. Metabolomic analysis and experimental validation focused on key metabolites and signaling pathways.
Compound 6a effectively inhibited proliferation and migration of breast cancer cells, showing stronger activity than panaxadiol and ginsenoside Rg3. Further metabolomic analysis revealed that the inhibitory effect of 6a on breast cancer cells was achieved by effectively regulating the "fatty acid degradation" pathway. Focusing on palmitoylcarnitine (PC), a key differential metabolite, we further analyzed its association with the DLL4-Notch signaling pathway. The results indicated that compound 6a interfered with cancer cell metastasis through the DLL4-Notch pathway and related metastasis signaling pathways, and further promoted the accumulation of PC. In in vitro validation, as the concentration of PC increased, it exhibited the same inhibitory effect on cancer cells as that of 6a.
In conclusion, this study systematically evaluated the inhibitory effect of the ginsenoside derivative 6a on breast cancer lung metastasis. This study not only provides insights for exploring the activity of panaxadiol, but also offers evidence for the application of ginsenosides in cancer therapeutic drugs.

papers.title: Fermentation of ginsenoside Rb1 by a probiotic mixture alleviates atopic dermatitis via synergistic effects of rare ginsenoside F2 and gut microbiota-derived 12-ketolithocholic acid in mice.
papers.authors: Yuan D, Walayat B, Chen X, Xiang D, Xing Y, Wang C et al.
papers.abstract:
Atopic Dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory skin disorder with increasing global incidence. Emerging evidence highlights a strong association between AD and gut dysbiosis. In this context, compounds from Chinese herbal medicine (CHM), such as ginsenosides, have gained attention for their anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties. However, the poor bioavailability of major ginsenosides limits their therapeutic effectiveness. Recent advances in probiotic-based herbal medicine fermentation suggest that, in addition to manipulation of gut dysbiosis, probiotics also show promising potential for enhancing the bioconversion of major ginsenosides into rare ginsenosides. The objective of this study was to determine whether probiotic-fermented ginsenoside Rb1 broth (Rb1FB) could alleviate 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene (DNCB) atopic dermatitis-like disease and to investigate the associated gut-skin mechanisms. Rb1FB improved visible skin lesions and reduced dermatitis severity and significantly reduced epidermal thickening, dermal mast-cell infiltration, serum immunoglobulin E (IgE) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) in AD mice. Rb1FB also increased gut microbial richness and diversity, enriched Bacteroides, increased fecal 12-ketolithocholic acid (12-KLCA), and enhanced systemic exposure to the rare ginsenoside F2. Therefore, the principal biological outcomes were improvements in the clinical-like, histopathological, allergic, and inflammatory features of AD, while the microbiome, metabolomic, and serum ginsenoside findings provided potential mechanistic explanations.
Probiotic strains Lactiplantibacillus plantarum DMU22441, Lactobacillus acidophilus DMU22440, and Lactiplantibacillus plantarum DMU22439 were screened for Rb1 utilization, and their fermentation conditions for maximum release of rare ginsenosides were optimized to prepare Rb1FB. A DNCB-induced AD mouse model was established to assess the therapeutic effects of Rb1FB. 16 S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene sequencing, metabolomics, transcriptomics and in vitro studies were employed to explore the mechanism of action.
Rb1FB significantly alleviated AD symptoms in mice, reduced serum IgE and TNF-α levels, modulated the gut microbiota, and increased systemic exposure to the rare ginsenoside F2. In TNF-α-stimulated HaCaT cells, combined treatment with F2 and gut microbiota-associated 12-KLCA produced greater suppression of selected inflammatory genes than either treatment alone and was associated with reduced NUAK family kinase 2 (NUAK2).
Rb1FB modulates the gut microbiota and its metabolites, enhances rare ginsenoside absorption, and alleviates AD symptoms in mice. F2 and 12-KLCA produced an enhanced combined inhibitory effect on inflammatory responses in vitro. These findings support the therapeutic potential of probiotic-fermented ginsenoside Rb1 for AD.

papers.title: Study on the anti-asthmatic effect of Ginseng-Schisandra herb pair and its mechanisms in regulating the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway.
papers.authors: Yang Q, Chen X, Cai J, Xie Z, Nie Y, Sun J et al.
papers.abstract:
Ginseng-Schisandra herb pair is a classic representative one of the "combination of tonification and astringency" in traditional Chinese medicine. Ginseng tonifies lung Qi and benefits heart Qi, while Schisandra restrains the lung, nourishes the kidney, calms the mind, and soothes the spirit. When they are used in combination, one can play a tonifying role and another can serve as an astringency, with tonification but without stagnation and with astringency but without depression, so the combination can not only enhance the efficacy of replenishing Qi and nourishing Yin but also strengthen the effect of astringing and consolidating. However, the underlying mechanism and action of its combined use in the prevention and treatment of asthma remain unclear.
An asthma model in mice was established by using ovalbumin (OVA) combined with aluminum hydroxide (Al(OH)3), so as to evaluate the anti-asthmatic effect of Ginseng-Schisandra herb pair and determine its optimal compatibility ratio. For further validation, an in vitro asthma model was developed by stimulating human bronchial epithelial cells (BEAS-2B) with interleukin-4 (IL-4) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α). The chemical profile of the herb pair extract was comprehensively analyzed by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS). Potential bioactive components and anti-asthma mechanisms were predicted through network pharmacology analysis and subsequently verified by Western blot and immunofluorescence assays.
Ginseng-Schisandra herb pair could improve the behavior of asthmatic mice, alleviate the pathological damage of lung tissue, reduce the levels of inflammatory factors in the serum of asthmatic mice and the asthma model BEAS-2B cells, increase the activity of superoxide dismutase (SOD), and decrease the levels of malondialdehyde (MDA) and reactive oxygen species (ROS). A total of 72 bioactive components were identified from the Ginseng-Schisandra herb pair extract, and the herb pair could inhibit the expression of PI3K-AKT pathway-related proteins in the lung tissue of asthmatic mice and BEAS-2B cells.
Ginseng-Schisandra herb pair can effectively alleviate the airway inflammatory response and oxidative stress injury by regulating the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway in mice to exert an anti-asthmatic effect. Among different compatibility ratios and compared with single herbs, the 2:1 ratio of the herb pair exhibits the optimal therapeutic efficacy.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Visual Needle Knife Release in Treating Knee Osteoarthritis: A Meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Pan H, Shi Z, Wu W, Wang X, Zeng W
papers.abstract:
To evaluate the clinical efficacy of visual needle knife release in the treatment of knee osteoarthritis.
Computerized literature searches were conducted in CNKI (China National Knowledge Infrastructure), Wanfang Medical Database, VIP Information, Chinese Medical Journal Network and PubMed. The search strategy combined subject terms and free words, including "visualization", "needle-knife", "needle-knife therapy", "knee osteoarthritis", and "KOA". Finally, randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of visual needle knife treatment for knee osteoarthritis that met the inclusion criteria were included for systematic review.
A total of 10 RCTs involving 739 patients were included in this study. The results showed that the clinical effective rate of the visual needle knife treatment group was significantly higher than that of the control group (OR = 6.00, 95% CI [2.87, 12.54], P < 0.001). In terms of WOMAC score, the treatment group was significantly lower than the control group (MD = -6.03, 95% CI [-8.79, -3.27], P = 0.001). Similarly, the VAS score of the treatment group was also lower than that of the control group (SMD = -0.72, 95% CI [-1.07, -0.37]). Additionally, the Lysholm score of the treatment group was higher than that of the control group (MD = 2.35, 95% CI [1.89, 2.82]). All the differences between the groups were statistically significant.
Compared with traditional blind needle knife, acupuncture, and intra-articular sodium hyaluronate injection, visual needle knife technique shows a higher clinical effective rate in the treatment of knee osteoarthritis. This technique is more effective in relieving knee pain and improving joint function, and is safer than traditional methods. Therefore, visual needle knife release is worthy of further promotion and application in clinical practice.

papers.title: Rapid Identification of Fritillaria Bulbus Botanical Origins and Adulteration by Thermal-Assisted Plasma Ionization Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometry Coupled With Chemometrics.
papers.authors: Qian C, Zou W, Zhao X, Liu J, Zhang W, Bi G et al.
papers.abstract: Fritillaria Bulbus (FB) is a valuable traditional Chinese medicine with diverse pharmacological activities. Due to economic incentives, high-quality FBs are frequently adulterated with morphologically similar counterfeit species in commercial markets. A rapid analytical method integrating thermal-assisted plasma ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (TAPI-TOFMS) with chemometric algorithms was developed and validated for the botanical origin authentication and adulteration identification of FB. Featuring simple pretreatment, high throughput, rapid detection, and excellent reproducibility, the established method was systematically verified by analyzing a total of 172 FB samples. Conventional chemometric analyses (PCA, PLS-DA, OPLS-DA) achieved effective sample separation based on botanical origins and different authentic-counterfeit adulteration pairs. The constructed PLS-DA and OPLS-DA models presented satisfactory explanatory and predictive capacities with reliable statistical parameters. Furthermore, three machine learning algorithms (RF, SVM, ELM) were adopted to build identification models for authentic FBs and their adulterants. All models yielded high prediction accuracies for discriminating authentic CBs from counterfeits (> 94.0%) and for the four FB adulteration pairs (87.5%-100.0%). Among them, SVM exhibited the optimal comprehensive performance in accuracy, prediction confidence, and model stability, while all three algorithms achieved perfect identification accuracy for the QB/XJ adulteration pair. Nevertheless, the method still has limitations in low-concentration adulteration detection, with a minimum detectable adulteration level of 20%, which is mainly attributed to the non-chromatographic separation characteristic of TAPI-TOFMS and the high chemical similarity between authentic and counterfeit FB species. This rapid and robust methodology provides promising technical support for the quality supervision and authenticity identification of commercial FBs.

papers.title: Network pharmacology and metabolomics reveal the mechanism of Qi Feng Gu Biao Granules against chronic bronchitis-related cough: a core role for the AGEs/RAGE pathway.
papers.authors: Fang F, Gu Y, Liu X, Liu X, Wang Y, Meng Y et al.
papers.abstract: Cough is a prominent and often persistent manifestation of chronic bronchitis (CB) that is frequently difficult to resolve. While Qi Feng Gu Biao Granules (QFGBG) is a traditional Chinese medicine commonly used to treat CB, its pharmacological basis for CB-related cough remains unclear.This study characterized the chemical profile of QFGBG by UPLC-Q-TOF/MS, evaluated its antitussive and anti-inflammatory effects in a rat model induced by lipopolysaccharide instillation combined with cigarette smoke exposure, and integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, Western blotting, and plasma metabolomics to explore the underlying mechanism.QFGBG reduced cough frequency, prolonged cough latency, improved body-weight gain, and decreased the lung index and wet-to-dry ratio. Histological analyses showed attenuation of lung and tracheal inflammatory injury and mucus hypersecretion. QFGBG also decreased the expression of inflammatory and cough-related factors. Network pharmacology identified 215 overlapping QFGBG-CB targets, with enrichment in inflammatory and metabolic pathways, including the AGEs/RAGE signaling pathway. Molecular docking suggested favorable binding of core components, including Formononetin, Acacetin, and Vanillin, to key targets. Western blotting confirmed that QFGBG downregulated AGEs, RAGE, p-STAT1/STAT1、p-STAT3/STAT3. Metabolomics indicated regulation of glycerophospholipid and arachidonic acid metabolism. These findings suggest that the active components of QFGBG may alleviate CB-related cough by inhibiting the AGEs/RAGE signaling pathway and regulating arachidonic acid and glycerophospholipid metabolism, thereby reducing pulmonary and neurogenic inflammation and the release of cough-related mediators.

papers.title: Phytochemical Profiling, Antioxidant Activity and Cytotoxic Potential of Chloroxylon swietenia DC. Stem Extracts Against Bladder Cancer Cell Lines.
papers.authors: Jambale U, Thimmappa SC
papers.abstract: Chloroxylon swietenia DC. is traditionally used in herbal medicine and is known to contain various secondary metabolites with pharmacological activities. This study includes qualitative and quantitative analysis of phytochemicals, antioxidant and anticancer potential of C. swietenia stem extracts. Stem extracts were prepared with chloroform, acetone, methanol and water. Phytochemical analysis revealed secondary metabolites, extracts were further analysed for total phenolic and flavonoid content, and bioactive compounds were identified by GC-MS analysis. Antioxidant activity was tested using total antioxidant capacity, DPPH and FRAP assays. Cytotoxicity was assessed on T24 cells using MTT. Methanol extract revealed the presence of flavonoids, glycosides, phenolics, saponins and tannins; acetone extract revealed the same presence of same secondary metabolites except saponins, leaving methanol extract with the highest diversity. Acetone had higher TPC (90.876 ± 0.964 mgGAE/g), whereas methanol had higher TFC (122.115 ± 0.962 mgQE/g). GC-MS identified the highest compounds in acetone. The highest total antioxidant capacity was 1.33 ± 0.02 (acetone). The methanol extract exhibited significant DPPH-scavenging activity with an IC50 of 119.080 μg/mL. Ferric reducing power was highest for methanol (0.75 ± 0.01). Acetone was most cytotoxic to T24 cells (IC50 17.131 μg/mL), followed by chloroform, aqueous and methanol. This study finds the presence of bioactive compounds in C. swietenia stem, which are potential natural sources with antioxidant and anticancer properties for further research.

papers.title: The 2027 BCPT Perspectives on Studies Involving Natural Products, Traditional Chinese Medicine and Systems Pharmacology.
papers.authors: Tveden-Nyborg P, Yang B, Albayrak G, Simonsen U, Lykkesfeldt J
papers.abstract: Natural products, including isolated compounds, complex extracts, traditional medicinal preparations and marine, microbial, fungal and animal-derived materials, remain important sources of therapeutic agents and pharmacological discovery. However, variation in biological source materials, preparation methods, chemical composition and experimental design may compromise reproducibility and interpretation. This guideline presents the requirements of Basic & Clinical Pharmacology & Toxicology for studies involving natural products and their semisynthetic or biotransformed derivatives. It provides recommendations for documenting scientific and ethnopharmacological rationale, taxonomy, authentication, provenance, sustainable and lawful sourcing, extraction, chemical characterisation, dosing, bioactivity, safety and data accessibility. Particular emphasis is placed on studying the preparation actually administered, using pharmacologically relevant concentrations and doses, controlling vehicle effects and assay interference and aligning mechanistic and therapeutic claims with the supporting evidence. Complex mixtures do not necessarily need to be reduced to a single active constituent; however, their composition must be adequately characterised, and claims concerning individual constituents, additivity, synergy or antagonism require experimental substantiation. Computational, network and systems-pharmacology analyses should be transparent and reproducible, with experimental validation of central predictions. These recommendations apply equivalent standards to natural products and other interventions while recognising the additional information required to define complex biological materials and improve overall translational relevance.

papers.title: UHPLC-HRMS-Based Tissue Pharmacochemistry and Metabolomics Reveal the Effective Components and Potential Mechanism of Huoxue Huayu Gel Plaster Against Oxaliplatin-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy.
papers.authors: Hua YJ, Zhang Y, Ding YJ, Chen JH
papers.abstract: Huoxue Huayu Gel Plaster (HXHYGP) is a topical traditional Chinese medicine preparation used for oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy (OIPN), but its locally exposed bioactive components remain unclear. This study developed an integrated strategy combining pharmacodynamic evaluation, UHPLC-HRMS-based tissue pharmacochemistry, untargeted metabolomics, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and qRT-PCR to identify effective components and explore potential mechanisms. In OIPN rats, HXHYGP improved mechanical and cold sensory dysfunction; reduced plantar tissue injury and inflammatory-cell infiltration; increased nerve growth factor levels; decreased TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β levels; and enhanced nerve conduction velocity. A total of 496 constituents were detected in skin tissue, including 20 tissue-migrant constituents attributed to HXHYGP. Untargeted metabolomics identified 53 OIPN-related differential metabolites, of which 42 were significantly reversed after treatment. Correlation analysis and network pharmacology further identified 14 effective components and 98 common targets, with EGFR, PIK3CA, MTOR, RELA, and MAPK14 as key nodes. Molecular docking supported potential component-target interactions, while qRT-PCR confirmed reduced mRNA expression of these targets after HXHYGP treatment. These findings indicate that HXHYGP may alleviate OIPN by modulating the proposed EGFR/PI3K/AKT/mTOR/NF-κB signaling network and MAPK14-associated inflammation. This strategy provides an analytical basis for identifying pharmacodynamic substances and potential quality-marker candidates in topical traditional Chinese medicine preparations.

papers.title: Management of Neuropathic Pain in Complex Regional Pain Syndrome: A Comprehensive Review.
papers.journal: Pain practice : the official journal of World Institute of Pain
papers.authors: Donati D, D'Auria L, Ricci V, Boccolari P, Tedeschi R, Tarallo L
papers.abstract:
Complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) is a complex and multifaceted condition in which pain may be neuropathic, nociplastic, nociceptive, or mixed in nature. This review aims to summarize the available pharmacological and non-pharmacological strategies for managing neuropathic pain in CRPS Types I and II.
Scopus, PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar were searched for randomized controlled trials, meta-analyses, case series, and case reports addressing the management of CRPS, with a focus on neuropathic pain. Studies were analyzed from the perspective of pharmacological and non-pharmacological approaches, with attention to differences between CRPS Type I and II.
Gabapentin (Level 1 evidence) and physiotherapy (Level 2 evidence) showed the strongest support among the treatments reviewed. Evidence remains limited or inconsistent for other pharmacological options (e.g., anticonvulsants other than gabapentin, opioids, antidepressants, ketamine, botulinum toxin) and for non-pharmacological interventions (e.g., mirror therapy, spinal cord stimulation, acupuncture). No significant differences in treatment efficacy were identified between CRPS Type I and II.
Given the complex and heterogeneous nature of CRPS, a multimodal, individualized treatment approach is recommended. Further well-structured studies are needed to strengthen the evidence base for the management of neuropathic pain in CRPS.

papers.title: Beyond regulatory recognition: Capacity building outcomes in traditional medicine South-South cooperation.
papers.authors: Wang J
papers.abstract: Capacity building dimensions of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) internationalization remain theoretically underdeveloped. This conceptual analysis introduces capacity building theory from development studies into TCM cooperation research, comparing the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Saudi Arabia under a most-similar-systems design across five capacity dimensions: institutional, talent, technological, industrial, and discourse. Both countries regulate traditional medicine, but their frameworks differ in kind rather than in scale. UAE licensing is administered at emirate level and accords TCM integrated-whole status alongside two other codified ethnomedical systems federally and in Dubai, and four others in Abu Dhabi, whereas Saudi Arabia licenses acupuncture as a discrete practice and accords that status to no codified system. Abu Dhabi licenses acupuncture separately as well, so whole-system recognition and practice-level licensing are not alternatives; the two countries differ in the presence of the former. Neither has developed commensurate capacity in local education, research infrastructure, or comparative scholarship. The broader recognition accorded in the UAE has not produced proportionately greater capacity elsewhere, which indicates that statutory recognition of traditional medicine practice is a necessary but insufficient condition for comprehensive capacity building. The analysis contributes to South-South cooperation literature by showing what capacity building theory brings into view that output-oriented assessment obscures, and identifies the structural dominance of biomedicine as a constraint across all five dimensions. Sustainable capacity outcomes require cooperation frameworks prioritising education system development and knowledge transfer, an emphasis consistent with the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Strategy 2025-2034.

papers.title: Effects of Nonpharmacological Interventions on Pain and Patient Satisfaction During Intrauterine Device Insertion: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.authors: Özcan H, Köksaldı E, Köse S
papers.abstract:
This study aimed to evaluate the effects of nonpharmacological interventions used during intrauterine device (IUD) insertion on pain and patient satisfaction.
This study is a systematic review and meta-analysis.
PubMed, Web of Science, EBSCOhost, Google Scholar and the National Thesis Center of the Council of Higher Education databases were searched between January 2026 and February 2026, without publication year restriction. Experimental and quasi-experimental studies evaluating nonpharmacological interventions during IUD insertion were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (RoB 2) for randomized controlled trials and ROBINS-I for quasi-experimental studies. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach. Publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots, Egger's test and Duval and Tweedie's trim-and-fill method. Data were synthesized using meta-analysis and narrative synthesis.
Twelve studies involving 1241 women were included. The interventions examined included virtual reality, distraction techniques, EFT, music, video-assisted information, ultrasound-guided IUD insertion, acupuncture, cold application and the full bladder method. Some interventions, particularly virtual reality, distraction cards, EFT, music and acupuncture, showed positive effects. Overall, nonpharmacological interventions significantly reduced pain during IUD insertion (SMD: 0.803; 95% CI: 0.427 to 1.179; Z = 4.182; p < 0.001; I2 = 90.687). They also significantly increased procedural satisfaction (SMD: -1.046; 95% CI: -1.516 to -0.577; Z = -4.368; p < 0.001; I2 = 85.677).
Nonpharmacological interventions may reduce perceived pain and improve patient satisfaction during IUD insertion.
These interventions may enhance patient comfort and procedural satisfaction in clinical practice.
PRISMA guidelines were followed.
This systematic review and meta-analysis was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) (Registration No: CRD420261307366).

papers.title: A 12-Week Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial of Salacia reticulata Extract for Fat-Mass Reduction in Adults with Overweight/Obesity.
papers.authors: Park SH, Lee JE, Bae SG, Kim J, Baek KS, Gwon Y et al.
papers.abstract: Salacia reticulata has long been used in traditional medicine for metabolic disorders, but clinical evidence for obesity-related outcomes remains limited. We conducted a 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the preliminary efficacy and safety of a standardized Salacia reticulata extract (SLE) on body-fat outcomes. Adults with overweight and/or obesity were randomized to receive SLE capsules or a matching placebo twice daily for 12 weeks. The coprimary endpoints were changes from baseline to week 12 in total body fat mass (g) and body fat percentage (%) measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry. The primary efficacy analysis was conducted in the full analysis set (mITT) using analysis of covariance with baseline values and sex as covariates. Per-protocol set analyses were performed as supportive sensitivity analyses. Among randomized participants, the mITT included 66 participants in the SLE group and 67 in the placebo group, and baseline characteristics were comparable. After 12 weeks, total body fat mass decreased in the SLE group, whereas little change was observed in the placebo group. The between-group difference favored SLE (ANCOVA-adjusted LS mean difference, -482.30 g; 95% CI, -907.05 to -57.54 g). The corresponding between-group comparison was statistically significant (Wilcoxon rank-sum test, P = .0158). Body fat percentage also decreased in the SLE group, but the between-group difference was not statistically significant (ANCOVA-adjusted LS mean difference, -0.30%; 95% CI, -0.73 to 0.12%; Wilcoxon rank-sum test, P = .1453). Several secondary body-composition outcomes, including trunk, android and gynoid fat measures, showed directionally favorable changes in the SLE group. In this 12-week trial, SLE was associated with a modest reduction in total body fat mass, whereas the second coprimary endpoint, body fat percentage, did not differ significantly between groups. These mixed coprimary findings provide only preliminary clinical evidence and should be interpreted with caution, particularly given the study's retrospective trial registration.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese medicine therapies for chronic nonspecific low back pain: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
papers.journal: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation
papers.authors: Ding J, Huang H, Wan Y, Fan M
papers.abstract: BackgroundChronic nonspecific low back pain (CNLBP) is a common clinical condition, and traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) therapies have been shown to effectively alleviate patient discomfort.ObjectiveTo evaluate and compare the efficacy of different TCM therapies in the treatment of CNLBP.MethodsA comprehensive search was performed in Web of Science, PubMed, Embase, and The Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials on TCM therapies for CNLBP. A network meta-analysis was performed to compare the outcomes of various interventions, with therapeutic effects ranked by the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA).ResultsMeta-analysis showed that for the Visual Analogue Scale, moxibustion (SMD = -2.08; 95% CI, -3.75 to -0.42; p = 0.0143), cupping (SMD = -5.69; 95% CI, -7.60 to -3.77; p < 0.00001), acupuncture (SMD = -0.94; 95% CI, -1.33 to -0.54; p < 0.00001), acupuncture combined with cupping(SMD = -6.65; 95% CI, -9.03 to -4.27; p < 0.0001), and traditional Chinese exercises (SMD = -1.86; 95% CI, -2.73 to -0.99; p < 0.00001) all showed significant effectiveness. The SUCRA ranking of effectiveness for these therapies was as follows: traditional Chinese exercises > moxibustion > acupuncture combined with cupping > acupuncture > cupping. Regarding the Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire, both moxibustion (SMD = -1.54; 95% CI, -3.00 to -0.07; p = 0.0397) and acupuncture (SMD = -0.79; 95% CI, -1.27 to -0.31; p = 0.0013) showed significant therapeutic benefits. The SUCRA ranking for these treatments was: moxibustion > acupuncture. Regarding the Oswestry Disability Index, acupuncture (SMD = -1.40; 95% CI, -2.54 to -0.26; p = 0.0159) showed a significant advantage.ConclusionTCM can effectively alleviate symptoms in patients with CNLBP through multiple mechanisms. Among these interventions, traditional Chinese exercises have shown the greatest efficacy in pain relief, while acupuncture provides broader benefits across various outcome measures.

papers.title: Effectiveness and Safety of Acupuncture for Cancer-Related Cognitive Impairment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.journal: Journal of integrative and complementary medicine
papers.authors: Zhang H, Liu J, He F, Ren K, Wang S
papers.abstract:
Cancer-related cognitive impairment (CRCI) is a prevalent and clinically significant sequela of cancer and its treatment, markedly reducing quality of life. As a core component of Traditional Chinese Medicine, acupuncture is a potential therapeutic intervention for CRCI; however, conclusive evidence on its efficacy and safety is lacking due to fragmented and methodologically limited studies.
This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of acupuncture for CRCI.
We systematically searched eight databases from inception to February 1, 2025, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in adults with CRCI comparing acupuncture with control interventions (e.g., conventional care, sham acupuncture, and other active therapies). Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane tool (v1). Meta-analyses used RevMan 5.3. Evidence certainty was evaluated with the GRADE framework. Prespecified subgroup analyses explored heterogeneity by acupuncture modality, treatment duration, cancer treatment phase, and cancer type.
Forty-four RCTs (n = 3,783) were included. Versus conventional treatment, acupuncture significantly improved Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores (mean difference [MD] = 2.34, 95% confidence interval [CI] [1.84, 2.85], P < 0.00001), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores (MD = 1.48, 95% CI: [1.15, 1.82], P < 0.00001), and reduced postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) incidence (risk ratio [RR] = 0.49, 95% CI: [0.41, 0.60], P < 0.00001). Compared with sham acupuncture, acupuncture improved MMSE (MD = 2.48, 95% CI: [1.55, 3.41], P < 0.00001) and MoCA (MD = 1.52, 95% CI: [0.16, 2.88], P = 0.03) scores, though the latter was imprecise. Acupuncture demonstrated no significant benefit for the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30 cognitive subscale compared with sham acupuncture (P = 0.11) or other active therapies (P = 0.15). Subgroup analyses identified treatment duration, acupuncture modality, and cancer type as major heterogeneity sources. Safety reporting was often incomplete, yet all documented adverse events were mild and transient. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation evidence certainty was low to very low.
Acupuncture may improve global cognitive function and reduce POCD incidence in CRCI. However, the safety profile requires further confirmation. Current evidence is limited by methodological weaknesses, substantial heterogeneity, and imprecision, highlighting the need for rigorous, high-quality RCTs with standardized protocols, objective biomarkers, and comprehensive safety monitoring to define acupuncture's role in CRCI management.

summary.methods: 성인 암 관련 인지장애 환자의 무작위배정대조시험 44편을 대상으로 침과 대조중재를 비교한 체계적 문헌고찰 및 메타분석을 시행했다.
summary.results: 침은 대조군보다 MMSE와 MoCA 점수를 개선하고 수술 후 인지장애 발생을 낮췄으나, 일부 삶의 질 인지영역에서는 유의한 차이가 없었고 근거 확실성은 낮았다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 암 관련 인지장애에서 침이 전반적 인지기능 개선에 가능성을 보이나, 근거가 낮고 연구 이질성이 커 임상 적용 시 신중한 해석이 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 연구의 방법론적 한계와 이질성, 불완전한 안전성 보고로 인해 근거 수준이 낮고 효과와 안전성의 확정적 판단이 어렵다.

papers.title: Effect of Acupuncture at HT-7 (Shenmen) and GV-20 (Baihui) on Anxiety and Cardiovascular Functions in Generalized Anxiety Disorder: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.journal: International journal of psychiatry in medicine
papers.authors: Dhanushya Devi G, Mooventhan A, Nivethitha L, Vijay A, Mangaiarkarasi N
papers.abstract: ObjectiveGeneralized anxiety disorder (GAD) is a condition that causes persistent and excessive worry, leading to physical and emotional symptoms. Acupuncture, a traditional Chinese medicine practice, has been studied as a potential treatment for anxiety disorders, including GAD. Though acupuncture at HT-7 and GV-20 along with other acupuncture points reduce anxiety level, no study to our knowledge has examined the effect of acupuncture at HT-7 and GV-20 alone on GAD. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to examine the effect of needling at HT-7 (Shenmen) and GV-20 (Baihui) acupuncture points on anxiety levels and cardiovascular function in patients with GAD.MethodsA total of 60 participants ages 20-55 diagnosed with GAD were randomly assigned to either a study group or a control group. The study group received acupuncture at the HT-7 and GV-20 points, while the control group underwent breath awareness meditation in supine position. Both groups underwent 20 min of the practice daily for 10 days. Assessments included Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A) score, blood pressure (BP) and pulse rate (PR), which were performed before and after the intervention.ResultsParticipants in the study group experienced a significant reduction in anxiety levels (P < .001) compared to the control group. No significant inter-group differences were observed in systolic BP (P = .686), diastolic BP (P = .998), or PR (P = .925).ConclusionThe present study suggests that needling at HT-7 and GV-20 acupuncture points (20 min/session for 10 days) reduces anxiety levels without affecting cardiovascular function in younger and middle-aged patients with GAD.
papers.title_ko: 범불안장애에서 HT-7(신문)과 GV-20(백회) 침의 불안 및 심혈관 기능에 미치는 영향: 무작위 대조시험

summary.question: HT-7과 GV-20 단독 자침이 범불안장애 환자의 불안과 심혈관 기능에 영향을 주는지 평가했다.
summary.methods: 20~55세 범불안장애 환자 60명을 무작위 배정해 침군은 HT-7·GV-20 자침, 대조군은 바로 누운 자세의 호흡 인지 명상을 10일간 매일 20분 시행한 무작위 대조시험이다.
summary.results: 침군은 HAM-A로 평가한 불안이 대조군보다 유의하게 감소했지만, 수축기·이완기 혈압과 맥박수는 군간 차이가 없었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 이 연구는 HT-7과 GV-20 자침이 범불안장애의 불안 감소와 연관될 수 있음을 시사하지만, 심혈관 지표 변화까지 뒷받침하지는 않았다.
summary.limitations: 단일 연구이며 비교 중재가 비침 치료이고 추적기간이 짧아 일반화에는 주의가 필요하다.

papers.title: Pure 6-paradol activates the TRPV1-PGC-1α-FNDC5-irisin axis in cultured myotubes, and a 6-paradol-standardised Aframomum melegueta K. Schum. extract reduces adiposity with relative preservation of lean mass in Korean adults with overweight: an integrated mechanistic and randomised controlled trial investigation.
papers.authors: Shim JH, Lee JY, Han J, Kim JH
papers.abstract:
Aframomum melegueta K. Schum. (grains of paradise; Zingiberaceae) is a West African spice used for centuries in the traditional medicine of Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal, and Cameroon as a warming digestive tonic and body-strengthening remedy. 6-Paradol, its principal phenylalkanone, shares the vanilloid pharmacophore with capsaicin, supporting TRPV1 agonism as a molecular basis for these properties.
To genetically validate the TRPV1-PGC-1α-FNDC5-irisin axis activated by pure 6-paradol in native skeletal muscle cells, and to assess whether a 6-paradol-standardised A. melegueta extract (AfperFit®) improves body composition in Korean adults with overweight.
In vitro (pure 6-paradol only): TRPV1 Ca2+ flux (HEK293-hTRPV1; native C2C12 myotubes); dual genetic knockdown (siRNA × 2; lentiviral shRNA); PGC-1α/FNDC5/irisin Western blot and ELISA; dexamethasone-induced atrophy; 3T3-L1 browning.
12-week randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (AfperFit® 500 mg/day; modified ITT population, n = 65 of 70 randomised). Co-primary endpoints: DEXA body fat percentage and visceral fat area; pre-specified secondary endpoints: lean body mass and serum irisin; exploratory bridge biomarkers: PBMC MuRF1/Atrogin-1 mRNA; ANCOVA with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction.
6-Paradol activated TRPV1 (EC50 = 0.71 ± 0.08 µM); lentiviral knockdown abolished ≥89% of the Ca2+ response and prevented PGC-1α, FNDC5, and irisin induction. Clinically, body fat percentage changed -4.2 vs. -0.8 percentage points (adjusted between-group difference -3.4 percentage points; 95% CI -4.5 to -2.3; d = 1.14) and visceral fat area -18.3 vs. -2.1 cm2 (-16.2 cm2; 95% CI -21.7 to -10.7; d = 1.31); both co-primary endpoints. Among secondary endpoints, lean mass showed relative preservation (-0.3 vs. -1.1 kg; +0.8 kg; 95% CI +0.03 to +1.57; d = 0.82) and serum irisin rose +42.6 vs. +2.5 ng/mL (+40.1 ng/mL; 95% CI +30.2 to +50.0; d = 1.67). PBMC MuRF1 mRNA, an exploratory biomarker, correlated inversely with serum irisin change in the pooled population (r = -0.61; p = 0.0003).
Pure 6-paradol engages a TRPV1-dependent irisin-secretory programme in cultured myotubes. In healthy Korean adults with overweight, the standardised extract produced large-effect adiposity reductions with relative preservation of lean mass and elevated circulating irisin. Because the clinical intervention used a multi-constituent extract, the clinical effects cannot be attributed specifically to 6-paradol, and the serum irisin and PBMC findings do not demonstrate activation of the TRPV1-irisin axis in human skeletal muscle; the in vitro-clinical concentration bridge is exploratory. Findings apply to healthy Korean adults with overweight (BMI 25-30 kg/m²; aged 20-50 years) and require validation in sarcopenic obesity and other populations.

papers.title: Chinese Herbal Medicine for the Treatment of Abnormal Uterine Bleeding: A Comprehensive Review of Molecular Mechanisms.
papers.authors: Zhang L, Zhang D, Shen W, Liu J
papers.abstract: Abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) is a highly prevalent clinical condition affecting women of reproductive age. Beyond causing severe secondary complications such as iron-deficiency anemia and infertility, AUB profoundly impairs women's emotional well-being, social functioning, and overall quality of life. Current mainstream guidelines typically recommend conventional treatments as first-line strategies; however, these approaches face significant challenges regarding long-term efficacy and patient tolerability. This unmet need has prompted both patients and clinicians to seek safer and more effective alternative therapies. Chinese Herbal Medicine (CHM) is widely utilized in the management of gynecological disorders, demonstrating remarkable clinical advantages in alleviating AUB symptoms, reducing recurrence rates, and improving patient tolerability. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the molecular mechanisms underlying CHM formulas and plant-derived bioactive monomers for the treatment of AUB, based on a three-tiered body of evidence encompassing clinical studies, animal models, and in vitro experiments. Current evidence indicates that classical CHM prescriptions and Chinese patent medicines primarily exert their therapeutic effects by rectifying endocrine imbalances, promoting structural repair of the endometrium, regulating systemic metabolism, and restoring coagulation homeostasis. Regarding CHM-derived bioactive monomers (eg alkaloids and flavonoids), their principal mechanisms are characterized by the inhibition of inflammatory cell infiltration, attenuation of oxidative stress, and suppression of pathological angiogenesis. Furthermore, they contribute to endometrial tissue remodeling through the regulation of abnormal cellular proliferation and the induction of apoptosis. It should be emphasized, however, that the mechanistic evidence summarized herein originates primarily from preclinical investigations. Robust clinical evidence targeting specific PALM-COEIN subtypes is still lacking and does not yet permit firm subtype-specific therapeutic recommendations. Moreover, available clinical evidence is unevenly distributed across AUB etiologies, and safety reporting remains inconsistent; these limitations should be considered when interpreting the clinical relevance of findings derived from animal, cellular, omics, or computational studies. Notwithstanding these limitations, the present review offers a coherent scientific framework for deciphering the "multi-component, multi-target" pharmacological paradigm of CHM against AUB and identifies critical avenues for subsequent research endeavors.

papers.title: Effects of Ultrasonic Conductance Acupoint Penetration of Dachengqi Decoction on the Recovery of Gastrointestinal Function in Postoperative Patients With Liver Cancer.
papers.authors: Li C, Chen Y, Xiao S, Wang L, Li Y, Hou X
papers.abstract:
Gastrointestinal dysfunction is a common complication in patients with liver cancer after surgery, affecting their recovery. The effectiveness of ultrasonic conductance acupoint penetration of Dachengqi decoction as a novel treatment method has not been confirmed in patients with liver cancer after surgery.
This study aims to investigate the effect of ultrasonic conductance acupoint penetration into Dachengqi decoction on the recovery of gastrointestinal function in postoperative patients with liver cancer and to provide experience for clinical reference.
In this randomized controlled trial, participants with liver cancer were enrolled from a tertiary hospital in Shandong Province, China. The control group (n = 38) received basic nursing measures, and the intervention group (n = 34) received basic nursing measures combined with ultrasonic conductance acupoint penetration of Dachengqi decoction.
Compared to the control group, the intervention group demonstrated a significantly shorter postoperative first flatus time, postoperative first defecation time, and time to initiation of food intake.
The application of ultrasonic conductance acupoint penetration of Dachengqi decoction can shorten the first postoperative flatus time, defecation time, and the time of food intake after surgery in postoperative patients with liver cancer.
In postoperative patients with liver cancer, ultrasonic conductance acupoint penetration of Dachengqi decoction is a secure and straightforward therapeutic approach that can effectively promote the restoration of gastrointestinal function. Future large-scale studies are warranted to replicate the study findings.

papers.title: Observation of the Clinical Effect of Auricular Acupressure in the Treatment of Insomnia: A SingleCenter, Single-Arm, Prospective Study.
papers.authors: Ma J, Zhang J, Xia L, Li Z, Wang J, Zhang H
papers.abstract: Insomnia leading to an inadequate fulfillment of the body's physiological sleep requirements in terms of both quality and duration. A single-arm clinical trial was employed. N = 84 and were given auricular acupressure treatment, 10 times as a course of treatment. The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), TCM Syndrome Score Scale, Insomnia Severity Index Scale, Flinders Fatigue Scale, Health Status Questionnaire, Patient Satisfaction Score and Auricular Temperature Change were filled in at the time of enrollment and after treatment, and the adverse reactions were recorded to evaluate the safety of treatment. According to the rate of reduction in the total score of the PSQI as the evaluation standard, 12 patients were cured, 46 significantly improved, 22 improved, and 4 showed no improvement, resulting in a total effective rate of 95.29% and a patient satisfaction rate of 90.58%, both showing statistically significant differences ( P < .05). So ear acupressure can effectively treat insomnia.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture Inhibits Hyperexcitability of Total Nociceptive Convergent Neurons in Subnucleus Reticularis Dorsalis Depending on Intensity in Inflammatory Muscle Pain of Rats.
papers.authors: Sun XY, Zhang ZY, Li YN, Zheng H, Chen JK, Su YS et al.
papers.abstract:
To investigate the inhibitory effects of electroacupuncture (EA) with distinct intensity and at different location of acupoints on total nociceptive convergent (TNC) neurons in subnucleus reticularis dorsalis (SRD) in rats with inflammatory muscle pain.
Anterograde tracer biotinylated dextran amine (BDA) was injected into the left spinal dorsal horn (SDH) of Sprague-Dawley rats to identify the ascending projections to the SRD. To induce inflammatory muscle pain, 200 µL complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA) was injected into the left gastrocnemius muscle of rats. In vivo extracellular electrophysiological recordings were employed to record the activities of TNC neurons in SRD. EA at 1 mA (A δ -fibre threshold), 2 mA (C-fibre threshold), or 3 mA (C-fibre suprathreshold) was delivered respectively to the ipsilateral Chengshan (BL 57), contralateral BL 57, or contralateral Shousanli (LI 10) of CFA injection site to examine the effects of EA on TNC neuronal activity.
After BDA was injected into the left SDH, labelled terminals in bilateral SRD were observed, indicating ascending projections from the SDH to the SRD. TNC neurons were classified as the neuronal population that responded selectively to noxious stimuli applied to diverse somatic regions. Stimulation applied in CFA-affected region evoked markedly enhanced discharges and wind-up phenomenon in TNC neurons (P<0.05). EA with intensity of 2 and 3 mA markedly inhibited nociceptive discharges and wind-up phenomenon of TNC neurons (P<0.05 or P<0.01), whereas EA with 1 mA exhibited no significant inhibition. Notably, EA with intensity of both 2 and 3 mA in different location of acupoints, such as ipsilateral pain region, contralateral region and extra segmental region, all produced comparable suppression efficacy (P>0.05). In addition, contralateral EA at 3 mA produced a sustained and stable inhibitory effect on the hyperexcitability of TNC neurons (P<0.05).
EA inhibited TNC neuronal hyperexcitability depending on C-fibre-activation without specificity of acupoint locations, thereby integrating nociceptive information with EA-induced afferent inputs.
papers.title_ko: 염증성 근육통 랫드에서 전침 강도에 따라 하부망상핵 등쪽부분의 총 통각 수렴 뉴런 과흥분성이 억제된다

summary.question: 염증성 근육통 랫드에서 전침의 강도와 시술 부위가 SRD의 TNC 뉴런 과흥분성 억제에 영향을 주는지 평가했다.
summary.methods: CFA로 유발한 랫드 근육통 모델에서 SDH-SRD 연결을 확인한 뒤, 서로 다른 강도와 침점 위치의 전침을 적용하고 SRD의 TNC 뉴런 활동을 생체 내 전기생리학적으로 기록했다.
summary.results: 2 mA와 3 mA 전침은 TNC 뉴런의 통각 발화와 wind-up을 유의하게 억제했지만 1 mA는 효과가 없었고, 침점 위치에 따른 억제 차이는 크지 않았다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 이 연구는 전침의 진통 관련 중추 억제가 침점의 위치보다 자극 강도, 특히 C-fiber 활성화와 더 관련될 수 있음을 시사한다.
summary.limitations: 동물의 신경생리학 연구이므로 임상 환자에게 그대로 일반화하기는 어렵다.

pico.c: 저강도 전침 또는 비교 가능한 다른 침점 위치
pico.o: SRD의 총 통각 수렴 뉴런 발화와 wind-up 억제

papers.title: Electroacupuncture alleviates chronic pain and comorbid depression through Gut-Metabolite-Brain axis remodeling to restore mPFC Glu/GABA balance.
papers.authors: Li S, Huang J, Lin D, Luo D, Fu W, Liu J
papers.abstract: The comorbidity of chronic pain and depression is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder involving dysregulated microbiota-gut-brain communication. Although electroacupuncture (EA) has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy for both pain and depression, the mechanisms linking peripheral microbial-metabolic remodeling to central neurotransmitter regulation remain incompletely understood. Here, we employed an integrated multi-omics approach in a spared nerve injury (SNI) rat model to investigate the gut-metabolite-brain mechanisms underlying EA's efficacy. EA significantly alleviated mechanical hypersensitivity and depressive-like behaviors while restoring mPFC Glu/GABA balance, accompanied by normalization of the glutamate transporter EAAT2 and the GABA-synthesizing enzyme GAD67. Metagenomic analysis showed that EA remodeled the gut microbial ecosystem by increasing microbial diversity, suppressing opportunistic pathobionts, including Bacillus cereus, Alistipes onderdonkii, while enriching SCFA-associated genera, including Butyricimonas and Romboutsia. These alterations were accompanied by coordinated remodeling of amino acid and butanoate metabolism. Correlation network analysis identified Pipecolic acid as a central metabolic node linking gut microbial alterations with mPFC GABAergic neurotransmission and behavioral recovery. Although individual bacterial genera did not significantly mediate its restoration, causal mediation analysis demonstrated that the Pipecolic acid-GABA axis significantly mediated improvements in both mechanical allodynia and anhedonia, supporting Pipecolic acid as a functional metabolic hub linking peripheral metabolic remodeling to central GABAergic regulation. Collectively, these findings identify peripheral metabolic remodeling as a key mechanistic interface through which EA coordinates gut microbial ecology and central neurochemical homeostasis, providing a systems-level framework for understanding the therapeutic mechanisms of acupuncture in pain-depression comorbidity.
papers.title_ko: 전침이 장-대사산물-뇌 축 재조절을 통해 만성 통증과 우울 동반질환을 완화하고 mPFC의 Glu/GABA 균형을 회복한다

summary.question: 전침이 만성 통증과 우울 동반 상태에서 장-대사산물-뇌 축을 통해 중추 신경전달 균형을 회복하는지 평가했다.
summary.methods: SNI 쥐 모델에서 다중오믹스 분석으로 전침의 장내미생물, 대사, 전전두엽 피질 신경전달 변화와 행동 효과를 조사했다.
summary.results: 전침은 기계적 과민과 우울 유사 행동을 완화하고 mPFC의 Glu/GABA 균형과 EAAT2, GAD67 발현을 회복했으며, 피페콜산-Pipecolic acid-GABA 축이 이러한 개선과 연관된 매개축으로 제시됐다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 전침의 통증-우울 동반질환 효과는 장내미생물보다 대사산물과 중추 GABA성 조절의 연계로 설명될 수 있다는 점을 시사한다.
summary.limitations: 동물모델 기반 기전 연구이므로 임상 환자에서의 재현성과 인과성은 추가 검증이 필요하다.

pico.p: SNI로 유도한 만성 통증과 우울 유사 행동을 보이는 쥐
pico.o: 기계적 과민, 우울 유사 행동, mPFC Glu/GABA 균형과 관련 대사·미생물 변화

papers.title: EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR framework reveals mechanistic insights of Buyang Huanwu Decoction in ischemic stroke with experimental validation.
papers.authors: Qiao R, Liu C, Pan X, Tian Q, He F
papers.abstract:
Buyang Huanwu Decoction (BYHWD), a classical formula recorded in Yilin Gaicuo, has been widely used for the treatment of stroke and post-stroke sequelae in traditional Chinese medicine.
This study aims to establish a novel framework based on the EWMCRITIC-VIKOR algorithm to prioritize potential BYHWD targets against IS by integrating multi-dimensional biological features, with validation through in vivo experiments.
14 biological features across 4 dimensions were quantified. Feature weights were calculated using EWM and CRITIC, and integrated via VIKOR for MCDM on BYHWD-IS overlapping targets. The therapeutic effects of BYHWD were validated in middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) rat model. Anti-inflammatory effects were assessed by RT-qPCR and ELISA, while western blotting were used to evaluate signaling via the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway.
The EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR framework prioritized 5 key targets (FOS, IL1β, AKT1, TP53, and IL6) from 239 overlapping targets. The VIKOR compromise solution exhibited a distinct low-Q priority set, in which the top targets jointly minimized group utility and individual regret, and the overall ranking showed weak association with logFC, indicating that prioritization was not driven by expression effect size alone. BYHWD treatment significantly improved MCAO-induced brain injury. RT-qPCR and ELISA showed marked downregulation of IL1B and IL6 after BYHWD treatment, and western blotting indicated altered PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling status.
The EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR framework enables robust prioritization of therapeutic targets by integrating heterogeneous biological data. This approach enhances mechanistic understanding of BYHWD in IS and offers a reliable strategy for target discovery in herbal interventions.
papers.title_ko: EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR 프레임워크로 본 뇌허혈성 뇌졸중에서 보양환오탕의 기전과 실험적 검증

summary.question: 허혈성 뇌졸중에서 보양환오탕의 잠재 표적과 작용기전을 다차원 생물학 정보로 우선순위화할 수 있는지 평가했다.
summary.methods: 보양환오탕-허혈성 뇌졸중 중복 표적에 EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR 알고리즘을 적용하고, MCAO 흰쥐 모델에서 RT-qPCR, ELISA, Western blot으로 항염증 및 PI3K/AKT/NF-κB 신호를 검증했다.
summary.results: 239개 중복 표적에서 FOS, IL1β, AKT1, TP53, IL6가 핵심 표적으로 우선순위화되었고, 보양환오탕은 MCAO 유발 뇌손상을 개선하며 IL1B와 IL6 발현을 낮추고 PI3K/AKT/NF-κB 신호를 변화시켰다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 한약 복합처방의 작용기전 탐색에 다중기준 의사결정과 실험 검증을 결합하는 접근이 유용할 수 있으나, 임상적 효용은 별도의 검증이 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 동물실험과 표적 예측 중심의 연구로, 사람 대상 임상 유효성과 일반화 가능성은 명확하지 않다.

pico.p: 허혈성 뇌졸중 및 MCAO 흰쥐 모델
pico.o: 뇌손상 개선, IL1B/IL6 감소, PI3K/AKT/NF-κB 신호 변화

papers.title: Clitoria ternatea as a phytopharmacological resource: plant metabolites, mechanistic evidence, translational prospects, and safety considerations.
papers.authors: Devi DR, Maheswari SN, Saranya RK, Aashritha S, Sankar NG, Gurrala NA et al.
papers.abstract: Clitoria ternatea L. (Fabaceae; butterfly pea) is used in traditional medicine and is increasingly developed as a food colorant, functional beverage, botanical preparation, and source of peptide scaffolds. Previous reviews have separately emphasized ethnomedicine, flower extraction, anthocyanins, or cyclotides; however, the evidence has rarely been integrated according to preparation identity, study design, bioavailability, safety, and translational readiness. This structured critical narrative review updates the literature through 8 August 2026. PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar were searched using species-name and domain-specific terms. Primary studies were prioritized, and evidence was stratified as chemical/analytical, in silico, isolated-target or cell-based, animal, and human. Study interpretation considered taxonomic authentication, plant part, extraction and chemical characterization, dose, controls, duration, model relevance, adverse-event reporting, and exposure plausibility. The principal metabolite classes are ternatin anthocyanins, flavonol glycosides, phenolic acids, triterpenoids, sterols, and cyclotides. Chemical assays such as DPPH and ABTS support redox characterization but do not establish pharmacological or therapeutic efficacy. Neurobehavioral, anti-inflammatory, metabolic, antimicrobial, organ-protective, and cytotoxic signals are reported mainly in preclinical models, often using incompletely standardized extracts. Human evidence is restricted to small acute crossover studies and exploratory adjunctive studies, including a 2026 study of flower tea in people with type 2 diabetes and diabetic distress. Intact ternatins are orally absorbed in rats, but systemic exposure is modest and human pharmacokinetic data are unavailable; metabolite exposure, formulation effects, chronic toxicity, reproductive safety, cyclotide immunogenicity, and botanical-drug interactions remain insufficiently defined. Recent genomic and peptide studies strengthen the biotechnology relevance of cyclotides and butelase-1 but should not be conflated with the efficacy of crude botanical preparations. Overall, C. ternatea is a promising source of defined food, botanical, and peptide products, but therapeutic claims require authenticated materials, marker-based standardization, exposure-linked pharmacology, and adequately controlled clinical trials.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese medicine-related interventions and the cGAS-STING axis in neuroinflammation: disease contexts and mechanisms of action.
papers.authors: Zhang C, Li Q
papers.abstract: Research on traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)-related interventions has shifted from overall phenotypic effects to defined neuroimmune targets. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) axis connects cytosolic DNA sensing with host defense and sterile inflammatory injury, but the functional direction of this pathway changes with disease context. This review organizes preclinical findings by pathological setting and site of action. It examines herbal formulas and natural compounds, followed by acupuncture, electroacupuncture, and related delivery systems. Several sterile injury models associate benefit with reduced pathway-related inflammation. Acute sleep deprivation provides an example of protection accompanying restored STING signaling. Early herpes simplex virus infection follows a different pattern: restoration of suppressed antiviral signaling improves host defense. In acute postoperative pain and cancer-induced bone pain models, increased STING-IFN-I signaling accompanies electroacupuncture-induced analgesia. Some interventions reduce mitochondrial DNA stimulation. Others act on cGAS or STING, with separate studies targeting STING trafficking. Downstream inflammatory and cell-death responses form the final level. Mechanistic attribution is strongest when genetic or pharmacological perturbation links pathway change to functional outcome; direct binding has been demonstrated for a small group of compounds. These findings support a context-sensitive framework for interpreting modulation direction that requires validation within individual disease models. Clinical translation will depend on reproducible formulation composition, effective brain exposure, and safety.

papers.title: Cumulative weight reduction across repeated acupoint catgut embedding sessions in obese women: a retrospective cohort study.
papers.authors: Ji X, Xin X, Li D, Hou L, Ye Y
papers.abstract:
Acupoint catgut embedding (ACE), a minimally invasive acupuncture-derived technique, is gaining popularity in weight management, yet high-quality evidence focusing specifically on obese individuals remains sparse. This retrospective cohort study was designed to assess whether ACE is associated with lower body mass index (BMI) in obese women and whether this association accumulates across repeated sessions.
We included obese women (BMI ≥ 28 kg/m2, aged 18-60 years) who completed four ACE treatments and attended five study visits (baseline and four post-treatment assessments) at Peking University Third Hospital from January 2016 to September 2025. An untreated control group of volunteers with similar baseline age and BMI was enrolled prospectively; their weight was recorded at five biweekly visits without any intervention. Baseline variables and serial BMI measurements were compared between groups using non-parametric tests.
Ninety-eight participants in the ACE group and 33 participants in the control group were analysed. The two groups were similar at baseline in age, height, weight, BMI, and waist circumference. By the third, fourth, and fifth visits, the ACE group showed significantly lower BMI than the control group (P = 0.043, 0.001, and <0.001, respectively). Within the ACE group, BMI at visits 2 through 5 was significantly lower than baseline, suggesting a cumulative association across successive sessions.
Some evidence from this study suggests that ACE may be associated with weight loss in obese women, with differences becoming detectable after two sessions and appearing to strengthen with additional treatments. No major adverse events were identified during the observed treatment period, supporting ACE as a possible adjunctive option for obesity care.

papers.title: Development and validation of an LC-MS/MS method for the determination of mycotoxins in the medicinal and edible herb dandelion.
papers.journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
papers.authors: Wang G, Tian C, Jiao M, Wang Y, Zhang X, Mohamed SR et al.
papers.abstract: Dandelion (Taraxacum mongolicum Hand.-Mazz.) is a medicinal and edible herb widely used in traditional Chinese medicine; however, studies on mycotoxin contamination in dandelion remain limited. Herein, we developed a liquid chromatography-triple quadrupole-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-QqQ-MS/MS) method for the simultaneous quantification of five common mycotoxins: aflatoxin B1 (AFB1), deoxynivalenol (DON), fumonisin B1 (FB1), ochratoxin A (OTA), and zearalenone (ZEN) in dandelion. The mycotoxins were extracted from dandelion herb, cleaned up by solvent dilution, and analyzed in multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) mode on an LC-QqQ-MS/MS system. Key parameters were optimized to achieve the best performance, including chromatographic conditions, MRM ion pairs, extraction solvents, and sample cleanup methods. Method validation was conducted in terms of specificity, limit of determination, limit of quantitation, linearity, intraday and interday precision, and matrix effect. Finally, a total of 54 dandelion samples collected from different regions of China were analyzed using the developed method. AFB1 and FB1 were detected in all the dandelion samples, while OTA was found in 45 samples. DON was detected in nine samples from three regions, whereas ZEN was not detected in any of the samples. FB1 was found to be the most prevalent mycotoxin in the samples, ranging from 9.77 to 35.86 μg/kg, followed by AFB1 and OTA, indicating co-occurrence of mycotoxins in this herb.

papers.title: Two active components, derived from dragon's blood, elicit a synergistic antitumor immune response in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.authors: Zhang S, Yan J, Tang X, Liu X, Gao S, Wang J et al.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a serious public health concern worldwide, and conventional therapies exert limited efficacy. In situ vaccination (ISV) activates antitumor immunity by inducing immunogenic cell death (ICD), making it a promising immunotherapy. Unfortunately, in HCC, a scarcity of mature DCs and dysfunctional vasculature collectively restrict ISV efficacy. Dragon's blood, a traditional Chinese medicine, is reported to exert potent antitumor effects. In particular, it contains anti-angiogenic agents (e.g., pterostilbene (PS) and ICD-inducing components (e.g., resveratrol (Res)). Therefore, we hypothesized that its antitumor activity may stem from synergistic stimulation of the antitumor immune response by its active components. However, the associated antitumor mechanisms of dragon's blood in HCC remain largely unknown. In this study, we first systematically screened active components with anti-tumor proliferation and ICD-inducing activities in H22 cells from several major components of dragon's blood in vitro. Res, identified as an ICD-active component, in combination with anti-angiogenic PS, was further evaluated in a murine HCC model to determine its antitumor effects and underlying mechanisms. Res induced ICD in H22 cells, and the combination treatment of Res and PS elicited a potent antitumor immune response in HCC. Further mechanistic research revealed that the synergistic efficacy of the combination therapy was associated with Res-induced ICD and PS-increased tumor hemoperfusion, which substantially promoted DC maturation and CTL infiltration, respectively. Overall, the synergistic stimulation of the antitumor immune response by Res and PS suggests their potential as an ISV-related strategy for HCC.

papers.title: Flavonoids From Sophora tonkinensis Disrupt STING-TBK1-IRF3 Complex Assembly and Ameliorate Inflammatory Diseases by Modulating cGAS-STING Signaling.
papers.authors: Wen J, Guo Y, Xu Y, Zhang G, Wang X, Song S et al.
papers.abstract: cGAS-STING pathway is a core regulator of innate immunity and inflammatory responses. Aberrant activation of the cGAS-STING pathway is closely associated with the progression of multiple inflammatory disorders. Flavonoids from Sophora tonkinensis (STF) are the main ingredients of this traditional Chinese medicine with definite anti-inflammatory activity, whereas its molecular mechanism against inflammation remains unclear. This work aimed to explore the regulatory effect and underlying molecular mechanism of STF on the cGAS-STING pathway, and verify its therapeutic efficacy on typical inflammatory diseases in vivo. BMDMs and human THP-1 were used for in vitro experiments. Western blot, RT-qPCR, ELISA, Co-IP, and Native-PAGE were performed to detect protein phosphorylation, gene expression, protein-protein interaction, and STING oligomerization. Lipopolysaccharide/D-galactosamine (LPS/D-GalN)-induced acute liver injury and LPS-induced sepsis mouse models were established to evaluate the in vivo anti-inflammatory and organ-protective effects of STF. Serum biochemical detection and gene expression analysis were carried out for in vivo sample evaluation. STF suppressed ISD-triggered activation of the cGAS-STING pathway, as evidenced by reduced phosphorylation of interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3) and STING, as well as decreased expression of downstream inflammatory mediators. Mechanistically, STF did not interfere with STING oligomerization but blocked the assembly of the STING-TBK1 complex and the interaction between IRF3 and TBK1. In vivo experiments demonstrated that STF dose-dependently alleviated hepatic pathological damage and hepatocyte apoptosis in a mouse model of acute liver injury. Furthermore, STF improved survival rates and attenuated multi-organ injury in septic mice by reducing the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines. STF exerts targeted anti-inflammatory activity via disrupting STING-TBK1 and TBK1-IRF3 complex assembly and inhibiting the cGAS-STING signaling cascade. It provides experimental evidence for the clinical application and translational research of Sophora tonkinensis and its flavonoid components in the treatment of cGAS-STING-related inflammatory diseases.
