papers.title: The effect of acupuncture-rehabilitation therapy on brain functional plasticity in motor aphasia after ischemic stroke: a randomized clinical neuroimaging trial.
papers.authors: Liu TT, Ren M, Wang J, Wang Y, Wang CJ, Tang Q et al.
papers.abstract: Motor aphasia is the most prevalent type of aphasia following ischemic stroke (IS). This study aims to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and underlying neural mechanisms of acupuncture-rehabilitation (A-R) therapy on motor aphasia after IS. Twenty-six patients with post-IS motor aphasia were randomly assigned to either the A-R group or the Conventional Rehabilitation (CR) group in a 1:1 ratio, and matched by age and gender with 26 healthy controls (HCs). The CR group received standard treatment and language training, while the A-R group additionally underwent scalp acupoint cluster acupuncture. Behavioral assessments and Blood Oxygenation Level Dependent functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (BOLD-fMRI) scans were conducted before and after the four-week intervention to evaluate therapeutic outcomes and underlying mechanisms. Compared to HCs, patients exhibited decreased Amplitude of Low Frequency Fluctuations (ALFF) in the right precuneus (p < 0.05) and reduced Regional Homogeneity (ReHo) in the left precuneus/postcentral gyrus (p < 0.05). Enhanced functional connectivity (FC) was observed in regions including the left Broca's area and right superior temporal gyrus, left Broca's area and right inferior frontal orbitalis gyrus, left Broca's area and right precentral gyrus, left Broca's area and right postcentral gyrus (p < 0.05). After intervention, significant improvements were observed in Aphasia Quotient (AQ) scores and sub-item performance in both patient groups (p < 0.05), with the A-R group showing greater gains in AQ and spontaneous speech scores compared to the CR group (p < 0.05). FMRI results indicated a significant increase in mean ALFF (mALFF) in the left inferior temporal gyrus after A-R treatment (p < 0.05) compared to before, and higher szReHo in the left anterior central gyrus compared to the CR group (p < 0.05). FC between the left Broca's area and right precentral gyrus decreased in the A-R group (p < 0.05). Additionally, a negative correlation was observed between the right anterior central gyrus and listening comprehension (r = -0.574, p = 0.020). The findings suggest that both A-R and CR therapies enhance language function in patients with motor aphasia post-IS, with A-R therapy demonstrating superior efficacy. The therapeutic mechanism of A-R likely involves activating left hemisphere brain regions, suppressing right hemisphere activity, and restoring hemispheric balance to facilitate functional recovery.

papers.title: AND-gate CRISPR/Cas13a-assisted colorimetric assay for dual microRNA monitoring of cervical spondylosis prognosis and auricular point pressing therapy evaluation.
papers.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
papers.authors: Wang Y, He W, Yang X, Zhang Y, Xu R, Liu Y et al.
papers.abstract: Simultaneous detection of dual microRNA biomarkers is crucial for accurate prognosis and treatment monitoring of cervical spondylosis, yet remains challenging due to the lack of stringent logic control and high-fidelity signal amplification. Herein, we report an AND-gate-controlled colorimetric assay that integrates target-recycling strand displacement amplification, CRISPR/Cas13a/crRNA-mediated trans-cleavage, and self-priming cyclic amplification for sensitive and specific analysis of two cervical spondylosis-associated miRNAs (miRNA-221 and miRNA-146a). Only when both targets are present does the cascade proceed, producing double-stranded amplicons that trigger SYBR Green I-catalyzed TMB oxidation, yielding a naked-eye-visible blue signal. The assay exhibits a broad linear range from 10 fM to 500 pM, a detection limit of 2.12 fM, excellent selectivity, and good repeatability. Importantly, we applied this method to clinically evaluate the therapeutic effect of auricular point pressing (ear acupressure), a traditional Chinese medicine intervention for cervical spondylosis. In a 4-week study of 20 patients, the treatment group receiving auricular point pressing showed significant downregulation of both miRNAs compared to baseline, while the control group showed no notable change. Results correlated well with RT-qPCR, confirming reliability. This logic-controlled CRISPR/Cas13a platform offers a robust, equipment-free strategy for early prognosis of cervical spondylosis and objective monitoring of auricular point pressing therapy.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture for Mild-to-Moderate Stress Urinary Incontinence in Women: A Systematic Review.
papers.authors: Shi J, Wu Y, Zhang Y, Li P, Li J, Xiao B et al.
papers.abstract:
Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) is a prevalent condition in women, characterized by involuntary urine leakage during physical exertion. Electroacupuncture (EA) is an effective therapy for SUI, offering minimal side effects, a low economic burden, and good patient compliance. To our knowledge, no systematic review or meta-analysis has specifically evaluated EA for mild-to-moderate SUI in women.
We systematically searched eight Chinese and English databases for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between 2002 and 2025. Methodological quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (ROB-2), RevMan 5.3, and GRADEpro GDT (version 3.6). Meta-analysis was conducted where feasible, while a qualitative systematic review approach was adopted for outcomes with limited data.
A total of 652 studies were retrieved, of which 10 met the inclusion criteria. The results indicate that EA may be effective in treating mild-to-moderate SUI in women, but the overall quality of evidence is limited and only two studies were categorized as having a low risk of bias, while the remaining eight were appraised as presenting "some concerns". Key limitations include small sample sizes, regional restriction to China, simplistic statistical methods in some studies, limited accuracy, and insufficient trial protocols.
Based on small-scale Chinese trials, EA appears more effective than sham EA, medication, or pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) in reducing urine leakage and improving ICIQ-SF scores, with superior long-term effects. However, due to limited, low-quality evidence restricted to Chinese populations, we cannot conclusively demonstrate EA's superiority over PFMT or pharmacotherapy for mild-to-moderate SUI in women.

papers.title: Efficacy of electroacupuncture for painful cervical spondylotic radiculopathy and associated changes in cervical biomechanical measures: a study protocol for a randomized, sham-controlled clinical trial.
papers.authors: Yu D, Lin F, Chen P, Zeng J, Lin W, Shao B
papers.abstract:
Painful cervical radiculopathy due to cervical spondylosis (painful CSR) is characterized by radicular pain and neurological dysfunction. Conservative care commonly includes medication and physical therapy, but evidence for individual nonsurgical interventions remains uncertain. Electroacupuncture (EA) is a non-pharmacological option, but rigorous sham-controlled evidence in painful CSR remains limited. This trial aims to compare the complete EA protocol with the selected SEA protocol and to characterize accompanying changes in prespecified cervical biomechanical measures.
This single-center, randomized, sham-controlled trial will enroll 80 participants with painful CSR and randomly assign them 1:1 to EA or SEA. Participants, outcome assessors, and the data analyst will be blinded. Both groups will receive identical standardized common care, with EA or SEA delivered in 20 sessions over 4 weeks, followed by 24 weeks of post-treatment follow-up. The primary outcome is the Week-4 Visual Analog Scale (VAS) score, analyzed with adjustment for baseline VAS. Supportive key secondary outcomes are the Week-4 Neck Disability Index (NDI) and Week-4 mean resting upper-trapezius shear-wave speed (SWS) on the primary symptomatic side. Other secondary outcomes include ultrasound- and surface electromyography (sEMG)-derived biomechanical measures, Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC), rescue-medication use, and the Short Form Health Survey (SF-36). Adverse events will be recorded through Week 28.
This trial will estimate the comparative clinical effects of the complete EA protocol relative to the selected SEA protocol and assess whether prespecified cervical biomechanical measures change alongside clinical outcomes. The findings may inform future evaluation of EA as a non-pharmacological treatment for painful CSR.
The Chinese Clinical Trial Registry identifier is ChiCTR2300075726.

papers.title: Effects of Needleless Transcutaneous Electrical Acustimulation on Gastrointestinal Function Recovery After Multi-Level Lumbar Surgery: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.authors: Song Y, Wang J, Zhang W, Li T, Mao Y, Chen JDZ et al.
papers.abstract:
: Postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction is a common complication of spinal surgery. This study aimed to determine the effect of transcutaneous electrical acustimulation (TEA) on the recovery of postoperative gastrointestinal function in patients undergoing lumbar surgery and to explore the underlying mechanism.
: Fifty patients undergoing multi-level (n ≥ 2) lumbar surgery were randomly assigned to receive TEA or sham-TEA treatment for 1 hour twice daily from postoperative day (POD)1 to POD3. Zusanli (ST36) and Neiguan (PC6) were selected as the stimulation points for the TEA group. The time to first flatus and defecation after surgery and other outcome measures were recorded. Gastric slow waves (GSW) were detected using an electrogastrogram, and autonomic function was assessed by analyzing heart rate variability derived from electrocardiogram recordings. Serum levels of interleukin (IL)-6, serotonin, and norepinephrine (NE) were also examined.
: Compared with sham-TEA, TEA significantly shortened the time to first flatus (P < 0.001) and defecation (P < 0.05) and reduced gastrointestinal symptom scores (P < 0.01). TEA increased the percentage of normal GSW (P < 0.05) and vagal activity (P < 0.001) postoperatively. Compared with POD1, TEA decreased the levels of IL-6, serotonin, and NE on POD4. Additionally, vagal activity on POD4 was negatively correlated with the time to first flatus (r = -0.383, P = 0.009). TEA treatment was identified as a factor independently associated with the time to first postoperative flatus and defecation.
: Needleless TEA is probably associated with accelerated recovery of gastrointestinal function after lumbar surgery, possibly through the modulation of autonomic activity.

papers.title: Modulating Th17-driven inflammation in ulcerative colitis with Chinese medicine: pathways, cytokines and beyond.
papers.authors: Tian Y, Yuan Y, Zhao Z, Li J, Xue G, Wang J et al.
papers.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a type of chronic non-specific inflammation of the digestive tract, whose incidence is increasing gradually. Th17 cells and their cytokines play a critical role in the inflammatory response of UC. Th17 cells need a particular environment for the production of cytokines and exert their immunoregulatory functions. They promote inflammation and tissue healing and interact with other types of immune cells. The abundance of Th17 cells and their cytokine expression capability were found to significantly change in the intestines of patients with UC. In this paper, we discussed how traditional Chinese medicines (TCMs) regulate the function of Th17 cells and cytokine expression in UC. Chinese medicine monomers (e.g., matrine, paeoniflorin, curcumin, etc.) and compound decoctions (e.g., compound Sophorae decoction, Gegen Qinlian decoction, QingChang-XiaoPi decoction, etc.) were shown to regulate the behavior of Th17 cells and their cytokine capability by modulating several signaling pathways. These TCMs inhibited cytokine secretion, improved the intestinal bacterial flora, restored Th17/Treg cell balance, and alleviated intestinal inflammation. TCM offers a wide variety of molecules that modulate the Th17 response and the development of UC. The use of these molecules, in conjunction with conventional treatments, may provide a better therapeutic option for UC.

papers.title: Tryptophan metabolism within the gut-brain axis in depression: mechanisms, association with heterogeneity, and therapeutic opportunities.
papers.authors: Qin Z, Lei T, Yi T, Zhang S, Tang Y, Xiang Y et al.
papers.abstract: Depression is a highly heterogeneous psychiatric disorder, characterized by substantial variability in clinical manifestations, treatment responses, and disease progression, thereby posing significant challenges to precision diagnosis and therapeutic intervention. Accumulating evidence indicates that dysregulated tryptophan metabolism, mediated through dynamic crosstalk with the gut microbiota and the gut-brain axis (GBA), plays a pivotal role in both the pathophysiology and biological heterogeneity of depression. In this review, we delineate the contributions of the three principal tryptophan metabolic pathways-the kynurenine, serotonin, and microbial indole pathways-in modulating neuroimmune signaling, neurotransmitter function, and gut-brain communication. Moreover, we synthesize current evidence demonstrating that microbiota-dependent tryptophan metabolism exhibits distinct profiles across clinical, demographic, immunometabolic, trauma-related, and genetically defined depressive phenotypes, thereby establishing its role as a unifying biological framework underlying depressive heterogeneity. We further provide a critical appraisal of emerging therapeutic strategies targeting microbiota-associated tryptophan metabolism, including pharmacological, nutritional, microbial, and traditional Chinese medicine-based interventions. Future investigations should integrate multi-omics approaches, longitudinal study designs, and mechanistic validation with artificial intelligence to elucidate causal relationships between microbiota-associated tryptophan metabolism and depressive heterogeneity, ultimately facilitating biomarker discovery and the development of precision therapeutics.

papers.title: Integrated UPLC-Q-TOF and serum pharmacological analysis: Yinchenhao decoction alleviates alcoholic steatohepatitis via inhibition of COX-2/PI3K/Akt and suppression of M1 macrophage polarization.
papers.authors: Wen J, Zeng Q, Wang Y, Chen T, Xie S, Kuang S et al.
papers.abstract:
Yinchenhao decoction (YCHD), a classic Traditional Chinese Medicine formula, has been widely used for the treatment of liver disorders. However, its therapeutic efficacy in alcoholic steatohepatitis (ASH) and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood.
To systematically evaluate the protective effects of YCHD and its bioactive compounds against ASH and elucidate the potential mechanisms through an integrated strategy combining UPLC-Q-TOF analysis and network pharmacology, with particular emphasis on the COX-2/PI3K/Akt signaling pathway and macrophage polarization.
The therapeutic effects of YCHD on lipid metabolism, oxidative stress, and inflammation were comprehensively evaluated using multiple experimental models. The chemical composition and material basis of YCHD were characterized by UPLC-Q-TOF analysis. Network pharmacology was subsequently employed to predict potential molecular targets and signaling pathways associated with the anti-ASH effects of YCHD. The regulatory effects of YCHD on macrophage polarization and the COX-2/PI3K/Akt signaling pathway were further investigated through COX-2 inhibitor celecoxib and COX-2 siRNA. Finally, the major active compounds were screened and experimentally validated in zebrafish, AML12 cells, and RAW264.7 cells.
YCHD exerted protective effects across multiple experimental models by improving lipid metabolic disorders, reducing hepatic lipid accumulation, and alleviating inflammatory responses. Phytochemical profiling identified 1,740 compounds in YCHD, including 195 blood-absorbed components. Network pharmacology analysis suggested that the PI3K/Akt pathway represents a critical target underlying the therapeutic effects of YCHD. Further validation demonstrated that YCHD reduced the expression of macrophage M1 polarization markers CD80/CD86 and decreased the production of inflammatory cytokines in ASH mice. Consistently, YCHD serum exerted comparable protective effects in LPS-stimulated polarized RAW264.7 cells by suppressing the activation of the COX-2/PI3K/Akt signaling pathway. Pharmacological screening further identified acacetin, apigenin, and fisetin as potential key compounds.
YCHD effectively ameliorates ASH by restoring lipid homeostasis, mitigating oxidative stress and inflammation, and suppressing M1 macrophage polarization through modulation of the COX-2/PI3K/Akt pathway. Acacetin, apigenin, and fisetin may represent important bioactive constituents contributing to the therapeutic effects of YCHD. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the pharmacological basis of YCHD in ASH treatment and establish a foundation for further identification and isolation of its active compounds.

summary.question: 음진호탕이 알코올성 지방간염을 완화하는지와 그 기전이 무엇인지 평가하였다.
summary.methods: UPLC-Q-TOF, 네트워크 약리학, 동물 및 세포 모델을 결합해 지질대사, 산화스트레스, 염증과 COX-2/PI3K/Akt 경로 및 대식세포 극성을 분석하였다.
summary.results: 음진호탕은 간 지방 축적과 염증을 줄이고 M1 대식세포 표지자와 COX-2/PI3K/Akt 활성화를 억제했으며, acacetin·apigenin·fisetin이 주요 후보 성분으로 제시되었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 알코올성 지방간염에서 음진호탕의 약리학적 근거가 전임상 수준에서 제시되었지만, 임상 적용 가능성은 추가 연구가 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 동물·세포 중심의 전임상 연구로, 사람 대상 유효성과 안전성은 확인되지 않았다.

papers.title: Stigmasterol Ameliorates Pulmonary Hypertension by Suppressing the CCL5/CCR5 Signaling Pathway: Taurocholic Acid as a Downstream Mediator.
papers.authors: Tang Y, Shi Y, Wang M, Cai S, Suo Y, Lu X et al.
papers.abstract:
Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a devastating disease characterized by irreversible pulmonary vascular remodeling (PVR), ultimately culminating in right ventricular failure and death. Although previous studies have demonstrated that stigmasterol (STG) reduces cholesterol levels and prevents cardiovascular diseases, its potential role in PH remains unknown. In this study, we investigated the therapeutic effects of STG on SU5416/hypoxia (Su/Hx)-induced PH in mice and elucidated the underlying molecular mechanisms.
Through bioinformatics analysis and network pharmacology, we identified STG as a promising herbal compound for PH treatment. Both in vitro and in vivo experiments validated that STG ameliorates platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB)-induced proliferation and migration of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), as well as PVR and right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH). Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, MM-PBSA calculation, and microscale thermophoresis (MST) were used to validate direct STG-CCL5 binding. Functional rescue experiments with taurocholic acid (TCA) were also performed.
Molecular docking, MD simulation, and MST revealed spontaneous direct binding between CCL5 and STG, with an MST-derived KD of 4.72 μM. While CCL5 promoted PDGF-BB-induced PASMC proliferation and migration, CCR5 inhibition counteracted these effects. STG ameliorated PASMC proliferation and migration by modulating CCL5. Furthermore, metabolomics and mass spectrometry analyses showed decreased taurocholic acid levels in lung tissues of CCR5-knockout (CCR5-/-) mice in the Su/Hx model. TCA reversed the protective effects of STG on PASMC proliferation and migration, supporting TCA as a downstream functional mediator.
In conclusion, our study demonstrates that STG ameliorates Su/Hx-induced PH by modulating the CCL5/CCR5 signaling pathway, with taurocholic acid acting as a downstream mediator. Further investigations are warranted to explore the clinical applicability of STG-based therapies for PH patients.

papers.title: Acupuncture for postoperative pain management and functional recovery after total knee arthroplasty in older adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Kou H, Liu H, Lai L, Yang S, Zhang X, Sun Y et al.
papers.abstract:
To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of acupuncture for postoperative pain management and functional recovery in older adults following total knee arthroplasty (TKA).
A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating acupuncture or electroacupuncture for postoperative outcomes in adults undergoing TKA. Primary outcomes included pain intensity (Visual Analogue Scale [VAS]) and functional outcomes (Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index [WOMAC], Hospital for Special Surgery [HSS] score, and range of motion). Secondary outcomes included analgesic consumption and adverse events.
Fifteen RCTs involving 1037 participants were included. Acupuncture and electroacupuncture were associated with reduced postoperative pain (VAS: SMD = -1.08, 95% CI, -1.27 to -0.89; Z = 11.09; p < 0.00001) and improved functional outcomes (HSS: SMD = 1.39, 95% CI, 1.02 to 1.75; Z = 7.48; p < 0.00001). No serious adverse events were reported in the included studies.
Acupuncture may provide beneficial effects on postoperative pain and selected functional outcomes after TKA in older adults. Given the multidisciplinary nature of postoperative recovery, these findings may be relevant to geriatric nursing care, particularly in pain assessment, rehabilitation coordination, and monitoring of recovery. However, the available evidence does not establish acupuncture as a nurse-led intervention.
papers.title_ko: 고령 성인의 인공슬관절 전치환술 후 통증 관리와 기능 회복을 위한 침 치료: 체계적 문헌고찰 및 메타분석

summary.question: 고령 성인의 인공슬관절 전치환술 후 침 치료가 통증과 기능 회복에 효과적인지 평가했다.
summary.methods: 무작위대조시험을 대상으로 침치료 또는 전침의 수술 후 결과를 분석한 체계적 문헌고찰 및 메타분석이다.
summary.results: 침치료와 전침은 수술 후 통증을 감소시키고 일부 기능 지표를 개선했으며, 포함 연구에서 중대한 이상반응은 보고되지 않았다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: TKA 후 고령 환자에서 침 치료는 보조적 통증 및 기능 회복 전략으로 고려될 수 있으나, 간호 주도 중재로 단정할 근거는 부족하다.
summary.limitations: 포함 연구들의 이질성과 제한된 근거로 인해 효과와 안전성 결론을 일반화하기는 어렵다.

pico.o: 수술 후 통증, 기능 지표, 진통제 사용, 이상반응
